text.p: Uganda's only Olympic gold medallist, John Akii-Bua, who died last week in a Kampala hospital, will be accorded a state funeral on Thursday, the government announced on Tuesday.

A statement from the ministry of internal affairs said Akii-Bua will be given full state honours and flags will fly at half mast across Uganda on Thursday -- which has been declared a national day of mourning.

The statement said Akii-Bua, a policeman who won the 400 metres hurdles at the 1972 Munich in 47.82 seconds -- a world record which stood for the next four years -- will be laid to rest at his home village in northern Uganda.
Akii-Bua, aged 49, died on Friday night after complaining of abdominal pains.
A programme released by internal affairs said Akii-Bua's body would lie in state in parliament on Tuesday for viewing by government ministers, diplomats and members of the public.
The body will then be driven by road to Akii-Bua's village at Lira in northern Uganda on Wednesday in readiness for his burial on Thursday at his native Abako village.

Akii-Bua was a native of Lango, northern Uganda, where the local sports stadium is named after him. A road in Kampala was also named after the athlete by dictator Idi Amin, who ruled Uganda in 1972 at the time of his gold medal.
Amin also gave him a house in Kampala but Akii-Bua fled from the country in 1979, the year Amin was ousted.
He was one of thousands of Ugandans, many of them from northern districts, who left when anti-Amin forces took over. He did not return until 1987.
Akii-Bua is survived by a wife and 11 children. He came from a polygamous family, one of 50 children his father had by nine different mothers.
